submitter: bugfix-036 thread (reviewer type slip voids whole council round)
rationale: bugs_open/036. A council round is lost — no verdict, no council_report, no objections returned — when ONE reviewer emits well-formed JSON carrying a field in the wrong register. Live: orchestration 5438f851-db9d-4f6a-bb32-3633e6793071 died at council_decide with 'cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field .objections.edit of type int', after every seat had run and been paid for. Measured over 14 days of complete_invalid runs: 3 of 5 council_decide voids are this schema-slip cause (the other 2 are the truncation cause bugs_open/019 already fixed). All 3 named the same seat, and all 3 carried a PLAN-LEVEL description in `edit` rather than a malformed index: 'plan-level (deploy verification)', 'risks note on the 54 mis-stamped rows', 'risks/summary (item 5)'. That is the key finding and it reframes the fix: those reviewers were not emitting garbage, they were saying the objection is about the plan rather than any single edit — which the contract already spells 0. json.Number (the obvious tolerant type) would NOT have parsed any of the three. Two changes, deliberately paired. (1) Make the `edit` pointer tolerant, mapping a bare index, a numeric string, and free text (to plan-wide 0), keeping the reviewer's own token verbatim so the persisted report is not laundered. (2) The structural half: stop a single seat's malformed output from voiding the round at all. bugs_open/019 already built exactly this seam for the truncation cause — salvage the opinion, else record the seat `unreadable`, which blocks an approval downstream. This extends that SAME mechanism to cover a seat lost to a schema slip, an unserialisable payload, and an unrecognised verdict, rather than adding a second parallel degraded-round path beside it (036 §7 warns that two independently-invented degraded-round paths in one function is the split-contract drift this repo files bugs about). The safety property the old hard error protected — a council that cannot read its reviewers must not wave a plan through — is kept, but enforced where it bites: an unreadable seat downgrades approve to revise, and zero readable opinions still fails the step. So the change can only ever make an outcome more conservative, never less. Sequencing note: 036 §7 said to wait for the 019 truncation work to land before touching this file, to avoid a same-file race. It landed (11a72dc31), and the tree is clean, so the gate is cleared.

plan.summary: One reviewer's malformed output must cost one seat, never the whole council round: tolerant `edit` pointer + route schema/serialisation/verdict failures into the existing `unreadable` mechanism built for bugs_open/019.

edits.rationale: Closes both halves. The `edit` field becomes a tolerant type (objectionEdit) that never fails to parse and preserves the reviewer's own token for the report; and the three remaining return-nil-err exits in the per-seat parse loop (planBytes failure, schema mismatch on VALID JSON, unrecognised verdict) are rerouted into the `unreadable` path that bugs_open/019 already built, via a new salvageMistypedReview sibling to salvageTruncatedReview. Deliberately NOT normalising an unrecognised verdict into the nearest legal one: guessing what a seat meant is how a veto becomes an approval, so that case records the seat unreadable instead of inventing a position for it. The len(reviews)==0 fail-closed guard and the approved+unreadable downgrade are untouched — they are what keep this conservative.

Covers the two properties bugs_open/036 §6 asks a fix to prove, using the three REAL payloads from the live voided rounds rather than invented ones. Also pins a subtlety found while testing: encoding/json continues past a TYPE error (unlike a syntax error) and keeps what did decode, so a mistyped `severity` costs that field and not the objection around it — an initial expectation of 0 objections was wrong and the test now asserts the better real behaviour.
